# Sirach Chapter 36 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 36 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_036_page_001.jpg

---

**36:1** Have mercy upon us, O Master, the God of all, and look upon us,

**36:2** and cast your terror upon all the nations.

**36:3** Raise your hand against foreign nations and let them see your might.

**36:4** As you have been sanctified in us before them, so be magnified in them before us;

**36:5** and let them acknowledge you, as we also have acknowledged you, that there is no God but you, O Lord.

**36:6** Renew signs and work further wonders, make glorious your hand and your right arm.

**36:7** Rouse your anger and pour out wrath, destroy the adversary and wipe out the enemy.

**36:8** Hasten the time and remember the oath, and let them recount your mighty deeds.

**36:9** Let burning wrath devour the survivor, and let those who harm your people find destruction.

**36:10** Crush the heads of the rulers of the enemy, who say, "There is no one but us."

**36:11** Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and restore them to their inheritance as from the beginning.

**36:12** Have mercy, O Lord, on the people who are called by your name, on Israel whom you named firstborn.

**36:13** Have pity on your holy city, Jerusalem, the place of your rest.

**36:14** Fill Zion with your majesty, and your temple with your glory.

**36:15** Bear witness to those who were your creatures from the beginning, and fulfill the prophecies spoken in your name.

**36:16** Reward those who wait for you, and let your prophets be found trustworthy.

**36:17** Hear the prayer of your servants, according to the blessing of Aaron over your people, and all who are on the earth will know that you are the Lord, the God of the ages.

**36:18** The stomach will take any food, yet one food is better than another.

**36:19** The palate distinguishes between game meats, and the discerning mind detects false speech.

**36:20** A perverse heart will cause sorrow, but a person of experience will repay him in kind.

**36:21** A woman will accept any man, but one daughter is better than another.

**36:22** A woman's beauty makes a man's face light up, and there is nothing more desirable than this.

**36:23** If there is kindness, meekness, and gentleness on her tongue, then her husband is not like other men.

**36:24** He who takes a wife enters upon a possession, a helper fit for him and a pillar of support.

**36:25** Where there is no fence, the property will be plundered; and where there is no wife, a man will roam and sigh.

**36:26** Who will trust a well-armed robber who slinks from city to city? So who will trust a man who has no nest and lodges wherever night overtakes him?
